svg.text: AML semantic layer: six layers, the files in each, and what reads them
Worked example: T0039 Circular Transactions (IND02191). L1 is reused external knowledge; L2–L5 are the semantic and data-access layers; L6 validates.
picks the technique from the L1 catalogue · writes SPARQL in L2/L3 terms (ids only) · writes the summary. Never sees a table or column.
and sub-techniques, their indicators, data sources
owner: AML business · names no database, no typology
7 the data can answer: FundsTransfer, Account,
owner: AML knowledge · draft, not reviewed
21 needsTerm: indicator → AML terms it needs
21 recordedIn: AML term → typology data source
(context only: no rule or verdict reads it)
owner: the data owner · changes with the database
No bridge line = the data cannot answer that AML
owner: engineering · the only layer that names tables and columns
R2RML maps: tx_features and kyc_profiles tables
SQL lens: declares tx_id unique (no self-joins)
owner: AML analytics + engineering · consumes layers 2–5
Verdict code: needs (L3) vs bridge (L4), failed rules
→ held · not held · facts only · cannot check
Guards: query terms checked, summary claims checked
L2 depends on nothing above it: it names no typology and no database
▲ L3 refers to L1 identifiers (indicators) and to L2 terms
▲ L4 aligns source terms to L2 terms (never to L3)
▲ L5 maps tables and columns to L4 source terms
▲ L6 reads L3 (needs), L4 (is there a bridge?) and the rows that Ontop returns
ONTOP 5.5.0 · reads L1–L5 in one run
T0039 → its 9 indicators and their text
never a column; the model cannot name one
“for each indicator, the terms it needs”
no bridge line → no rows, no error
table tx_features, one row per transfer
never copied into an RDF store
no country, no raw amount, no invoice
Held together by checks, not by convention
src/paths.py names every file once · src/sources.py: a needed term must be recorded in a data source of its technique, every source must exist in L1, every bridged term
must be provided by a table (L5) · tests/test_modules.py: each file sits in its layer’s folder · everything in L2–L5 is a draft reading, not reviewed by a domain expert.
